# Testing examples

The null hypothesis, the test statistic, the p-value, and the type I and type II errors are defined in [Hypothesis tests](inf-04-hypothesis-tests.qmd). A p-value is not the probability that the null hypothesis is true. That probability, when it is the quantity wanted, is a posterior probability, computed in [Bayesian hypotheses and model comparison](bayes-06-testing.qmd).

The examples here are the one-sample $t$ test, the one-sample test for a proportion, and the two-sample versions of both. The interval that often sits next to the test is the one in [Confidence intervals](inf-03-confidence-intervals.qmd).

## Exercises

::: {#ex-da-caffeine-cola .exercise}
## Caffeine in a cola

A brand of cola is sampled $n=40$ times. The mean caffeine is 19.57 mg per 6 oz serving and the sample standard deviation is 1.40 mg. The claim under test is that the mean is 19 mg, against the alternative that it is higher.

(a) State the model and the two hypotheses.

(b) Give the test statistic and its null distribution.

(c) Compute the observed statistic, the one-sided p-value, and the decision at level 0.05. Use the fact that the upper tail of $t_{39}$ beyond 2.57 is about 0.007.

[Solution](#sol-da-caffeine-cola)

:::

::: {#ex-da-brexit-poll .exercise}
## A later poll on leaving

A referendum split 51.9% leave and 48.1% remain. A later sample of 500 people has 54% preferring to remain, so 46% preferring to leave. Test whether the leave proportion is still 0.519, against a two-sided alternative.

The standardised statistic is $z=-2.64$, and the two-sided standard-normal tail beyond 2.64 is about 0.0082. Also give an approximate 95% confidence interval for the leave proportion in the later poll.

[Solution](#sol-da-brexit-poll)

:::

::: {#ex-da-steel-rods .exercise}
## Steel rod diameters

Rods should be at least 6 cm in diameter. A sample of 100 rods has mean 6.1 cm and standard deviation 0.1 cm. Assume a normal model.

(a) Estimate the probability that a single rod is thinner than 6 cm.

(b) If the standard deviation stays 0.1 cm, what mean diameter makes 99% of rods at least 6 cm? Use $z_{0.99}=2.326$.

(c) Test $H_0:\mu=6$ against $H_1:\mu>6$. The observed $t$ statistic on 99 degrees of freedom is enormous. What is the conclusion?

[Solution](#sol-da-steel-rods)

:::

::: {#ex-da-shuffle .exercise}
## A shuffling machine

Twenty fresh packs are shuffled. Seventeen have a red card on top. Test whether the top card is still equally likely to be red or black, against the alternative that red is more likely than $1/2$. The one-sided binomial p-value is 0.00174.

[Solution](#sol-da-shuffle)

:::

::: {#ex-da-two-proportions .exercise}
## Two proportions

Independent samples give $\widehat p_X$ and $\widehat p_Y$. The test of $H_0:p_X=p_Y$ against $H_1:p_X>p_Y$ has p-value 0.23. An approximate 99% confidence interval for $p_X-p_Y$ is $(-0.067,\,0.121)$.

(a) State the hypotheses.

(b) What does the p-value say at level 0.05?

(c) Does the interval contain 0?

[Solution](#sol-da-two-proportions)

:::

::: {#ex-da-home-ground .exercise}
## Home-ground wins

Of 25 home games, 20 were wins. Of 75 away games, 55 were wins. Each game is an independent Bernoulli trial, with a probability that depends only on home or away. The two-sample test of equal win probabilities has p-value 0.2526.

State the hypotheses and the conclusion at level 0.05.

[Solution](#sol-da-home-ground)

:::
